precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness” is not talking about all people. The man is Adam, and verse 28 shows it: God blessed them and told them to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” That is Adam and the line coming from him, which would eventually be the twelve tribes of Israel.

Genesis 2:7 is read together with it: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” Formed from the dust of the ground: we know God is black, Christ is black and the apostles were black. The real Jews are black, and the Caucasian race, Esau as the Bible calls them, is cursed.

Solomon says the same in Wisdom of Solomon 7, that he is “the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”, and that God gave him to know “the operation of the elements.” The elements in the soil are the elements in man: oxygen, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, in different percentages. When God made us from the dust, he took from those elements and worked them to form man, the way he formed land and sea. That is what we call the periodic table today, and it is what Esau tries to do with his so-called science: play Frankenstein and try to become God.

But the image goes deeper than the dust and the skin. The breath God breathed in is wisdom, “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” He gave it to us so that we would know better. Being made after his image and likeness is his spirit, the commandments of God.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:24
precepts.why:
After his image and after his likeness means his spirit, the commandments of God. A lot of the time people think the image and likeness only means looking like God. Ephesians 4:24 shows what his image is: “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

That is after the image of God: created in righteousness. The man God made in his image was made to be righteous and holy, not only to share his color.

So being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; you are still the devil. We say the white man is a devil, but there are black devils too. Just because you are black does not make you special unless you are righteous. It is the laws of God that make us special.

precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Genesis says “after our likeness”, and Psalms 17:15 shows what that likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is righteousness. David beholds God's face in righteousness and is satisfied to wake in his likeness. So man made after God's image and likeness was meant to be righteous.

Read with Ephesians 4:24, the new man “created in righteousness and true holiness”, it is plain: black is black, but being made in his image means being black and righteous, because black and wicked ain't the way to go: you're still the devil. We say the white man's a devil, but there's black devils too. Just because you are black don't make you special unless you are righteous; it is the laws of God that make us special. The dust of the ground made the body; keeping the commandments is what makes us his likeness.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:5-8
precepts.why:
At the golden calf “the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.” What was that rose up to play? You think it was hopscotch? Paul explains it.

“Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” He is quoting the very verse, and before it he says: “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” When they lusted after evil things, that is the rose up to play.

The verse before that: “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” Why were they overthrown in the wilderness? Because they lusted after evil things.

Then verse 8: “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” So we understand the rose up to play was fornication. They lusted after evil things, and it destroyed us.

The nations understood this. When we are in sin, they know what will happen, they can destroy us. So when they took their crafty counsel they said, how do we keep these people in error? They like to rap, so give them murder music and lascivious music. That is why they give our sisters these songs, so vulgar. Their whole plan is to keep us in sin. Pleasure now, regret later: you are going to pay.

precepts.label: Numbers 25:18
precepts.why:
“the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” “And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.” What would cause us to bow down to their gods? It just says they committed whoredom. It was sex that got the people to worship another god, and “Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.”

Jump to the end of the chapter: “For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor”. They vex you with their wiles, their seduction, and beguiled you into worshipping their gods. They knew: we have to get these people to sin against their God. So they used this tricknology, this stratagem, to move them away from God. That was the popular plan. “and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, which was slain in the day of the plague for Peor’s sake.”

“For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world”. It was Moab then, and it is all the nations now. Today the majority of the pornography is controlled by Amalek and Edom. They understood: we are going to destroy the minds of the people. We are not the only race having sex, but all our music is derogatory and evil, every video is a twerk video, and even somebody’s grandmother is twerking online. Everything is over-sexualized to destroy the minds of our young people, along with the drugs, the whoring and the music.

These are the wiles of the devil. The Lord would not let Balaam curse Israel, so the counsel was to make Israel fall through whoredom. As long as we continue in whoredom we will not build healthy marriages, we will not produce spiritually healthy children, and the generational curses keep going. Our strength is to come back to the laws of God.

precepts.label: Romans 8:16
precepts.why:
“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed”. I don't care what country you are in, what state, what continent: these curses are following us. That's why we're getting shot down in the streets and killed left and right; the Most High has to do something to wake us back up. We are a destroyed nation, and we haven't understood that yet.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”. The curses are the sign. That is how we know we are the Israelites: the Bible gives us the signs to look out for, in Deuteronomy 28:15-68 and in Genesis 49, and if our spirit resonates with those signs, we are going to realize that we are the Israelites.

That is Romans 8:16: “The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”. That we, the Israelites, are the children of God. Not the whole world. The spirit itself, the Bible, bears witness with our spirit that we are those children.

And “for a wonder”: we are supposed to be wondering what happened. We are the greatest people on earth; how did we get so low? It will be upon our seed for ever, upon our children until Christ's return. Brothers want to argue the trinity while our people are being killed, holding the name Israel and refusing everything that goes with it. The sign is on us, and the spirit bears witness with ours: we are Israel, and we have to come back to the Lord.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:32
precepts.why:
“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: in chattel slavery our lives were in doubt every day. Every day there was a chance we would be killed, a chance we might get lynched. And not only the lives of the mothers and fathers were in doubt; our sons were in doubt too. That is why verse 32 is read here: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people.”

That could have happened at any moment, any day. Your son ripped out of your arms to be sold to Master so-and-so, and you would never see your children again. From the day that child was born until the day someone said, I want that one as a slave, the parents lived with it, and they had nothing to say about it. “and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”: they watched their sons get taken away and watched their daughters get taken away. That is the failing of eyes and the sorrow of mind of verse 65: no way to change your reality, no future you can see for your children.

“and there shall be no might in thine hand”: no might in our hands to stop it. And there was no alcohol for them. A bottle of whiskey would not have stopped that. They had to endure this thing sober, knowing the Lord was still going to be with us somehow, some way. So they could not off themselves, because a generation was going to come from them, from the wife and from the husband, and our seed would continue while they went through trauma after trauma.

It took faith to make it from morning to night and night to morning, and they did not even have the truth the way we know it today. They pushed through all that evil and ugliness so that you and I could sit here today. So what excuse do we have? We cannot leave our post to drink and get high, or put our head inside a bottle and a crack pipe, when our forefathers endured this and kept pushing.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 4:13
precepts.why:
Who was the Lord talking to in 2 Chronicles 7? Solomon. “if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked”, and “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes”, then “will I pluck them up by the roots”. So what was Solomon's problem, outside of the sin itself? Solomon tells it on himself: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.”

That was his problem. He couldn't take correction. He didn't want to hear it; nobody could tell him nothing. That's like some brothers here: they can't be told, they don't want to hear it, they get offended. He was an old, foolish king who could no longer be admonished, and from that trickled all the other problems he had.

Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: to fear God and keep his commandments. But he shouldn't have had to go through that. All wisdom was given to him, and he saw his father's life before his eyes. He was concerned with how the world operated and wanted to experience the world, when we are supposed to be unspotted from this world.

So the forsaking that brought the captivity began with a king who could not be admonished. When you keep repeating something to people who can't be told anything, after a while you lose them. That is why we have to be willing to receive correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 15:10
precepts.why:
The Lord warned Solomon, “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments”; to forsake means to abandon, desert or leave something entirely, a breach of duty, to totally turn your back. Proverbs ties forsaking to hating correction: “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.”

When you have forsaken the way, being corrected is grievous to you. You keep having to be told the same thing over and over, and the one who doesn't want to hear it gets pissed off; he doesn't want to hear it no more. That was Solomon, the old and foolish king who would no more be admonished.

And the end of it is death: “he that hateth reproof shall die.” For Israel it meant being plucked up by the roots out of the land and made a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we are in captivity today. We got jammed up because we would not take correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
“He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” Often reproved means every time the correction comes, he will not accept it. So he gets corrected over and over, and after a while his neck becomes hardened. He becomes stiffnecked. The scriptures don't have that effect on him anymore; there is no contriteness, no shame. You see brothers always getting stood up, and after a while it's, yeah, okay, put me out, I'll be back.

Why does that happen? The word of God is not moving you to change. You can't be the same person you were before; there has to be some type of growth. How do you find yourself doing the same thing you were doing ten years ago? Why, ten years later, does somebody have to motivate you to go do the work? Something is not firing off; something is disconnected.

The word of God is supposed to inspire you to change. The word of God changes you; the word of God can cure you. If you ain't changing, it is one of two things: you are a heathen, or you are a reprobate, and the kingdom ain't for you. So if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.

That is the other side of 2 Chronicles 7:14. The Lord will hear and forgive and heal the land when his people humble themselves and turn from their wicked ways. The one who hardens his neck against reproof is suddenly destroyed, and that without remedy.

precepts.label: Job 36:15
precepts.why:
Job 36:10 says the Lord “openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity”: he commanded, requested and called you to return from iniquity back to your heritage. Verse 15 shows where he opens those ears: “He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.”

The poor here are our people. It was through the oppression of the oppressor, and through the religion he gave us, that our ears were opened. Esau is not poor. They are rich through robbery, and that continues to this day. We are a people robbed and spoiled and hid in prison houses, as Isaiah 42 says, and it is being played out in real time.

Just because you are not in the prison system doesn't mean you are not in captivity. Deuteronomy 28:15-68 applies to us: the Lord gave us the warning, we didn't take heed, and the curses are in full effect. The 13th Amendment was supposed to end slavery, but its clause, except as punishment for crime, made the loophole that fills the prisons with our people for free labor. Slavery was never abolished; it evolved. They framed mischief and made it law, like the throne of iniquity that “frameth mischief by a law.” A warden speaks of a young man's sweat equity instead of the death penalty, the same spirit as the Willie Lynch letter: don't kill him, it's not good economics.

This is still the land of our captivity, and the enemy got crafty with us. But in that oppression the Lord opened our ears. We were deaf and now we hear discipline; we were blind and now we see. We are not supposed to be at rest in this land. Your 9-to-5 is not your purpose; your purpose is to keep his commandments, remember that you are called and requested of God, and magnify his law upon the earth.

precepts.label: Isaiah 48:17
precepts.why:
“O my God, I trust in thee: let me not be ashamed, let not mine enemies triumph over me.” Then: “Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.” Look at what David is asking for: lead me and teach me.

Isaiah shows how God answers that: “Thus saith the Lord, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the Lord thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.” He leads you by the way, in the direction you should go.

And God leads through the prophets he sends, and many of them were killed. People hate the word of God so much that they want to kill us. That's why it says be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath. The brothers go out to teach and get guns pulled on them, just for reading the Bible, while dudes drive by selling crack, fentanyl, whatever they sell. Guns pulled on us by Christian folk. That's why the church can't be stood: church is full of crap.

So are we the enemies because we tell the people the truth? No. You're just simple and you don't want correction. We are going to do our job and teach you the good and the right way, and keep our hands clean. What you do with it is on you. Either repent, or die in your sins.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 19:13-15
precepts.why:
The wicked of Psalms 50 hates instruction and casts God's words behind him, and “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Sirach shows the right way to deal with a brother or friend: “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.”

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

So why do we sit and speak against our brother? Because sometimes a brother admonishes you, and now you are angry behind it. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you? Admonishing is what a friend is supposed to do. The one who hates instruction turns the admonishment around and slanders the brother who gave it.

God says to that man, “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”. Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you are going to get away with it.

precepts.label: Proverbs 18:24
precepts.why:
Why is a friend's admonishment the same matter as speaking against your brother? Because friend and brother are synonymous. Proverbs explains it: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.”

There are some friends that are closer than a brother. So when Psalms 50:20 says “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”, the slander lands on the friend who admonished you as much as on your own blood.

A man that has friends must show himself friendly, not turn on the friend who corrects him. And God will not keep silence forever: “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” That is Israel, because the other nations never knew God to forget him. “and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God”, and the salvation is only to Israel.

precepts.label: Judith 5:11
precepts.why:
The psalm says of the nations, “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” Who are God's people? We are God's people. And Judith shows one of their crafty counsels from the beginning: “Therefore the king of Egypt rose up against them, and dealt subtilly with them, and brought them low with labouring in brick, and made them slaves.”

That is one of their crafty counsels: we are going to work them to death. Today many of our people are working two big jobs, living paycheck to paycheck, too poor to stop working. It is happening even more with Trump in office. There is no middle class; that thing is gone. You can't work for a living wage and survive out here.

There was a time, and some of you older people understand, when you could have a job delivering milk or eggs, or work in a post office, and buy a home on one salary. Not no more. People with full-time jobs making $50,000 a year in LA are homeless, living in storage units.

They said, we have to find ways to keep the children of Israel under our foot. If we can't get them in religion, we will get them in the workforce. If not the workforce, gangs; if not gangs, porn; we will turn them into criminals. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, confederate with one consent, to cut Israel off from being a nation. In this world, all we have got is us.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:42
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra, “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” God's judgment goes round like a ring, a wheel. It comes around without fail, the last no slower than the first.

The scriptures say God shall be known in his judgments. So when Deuteronomy says that when we sin we will find ourselves back in captivity, in slavery and in prison houses, and we look around and see those conditions, his judgment stands. It is sure, and his prophecies are fulfilled. That is how we show that God is here: so take heed and fear God.

That is the frame for Psalms 94:20: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” The 13th Amendment abolished slavery except as punishment for crime. Within fifteen years the Southern states were imprisoning black Americans at ten times the rate of whites; they made loitering and vagrancy felonies and leased the convicts out for forced labor. Today prison labor makes billions while inmates earn cents an hour. They framed mischief by a law and misled us with democracy and freedom. Slavery did not end; it evolved.

A former warden testified that a young defendant should get life without parole instead of death because the prison could use him: he is young, he is healthy, we need that sweat equity. That is the Willie Lynch letter: beat him within an inch of his life but don't kill him, because it is not good for economics.

The throne of iniquity has no fellowship with Christ: not their holidays, not their man-made religions, and no, the president is not God. Some people do need to be locked up if they rob and steal. But the judgment keeps turning like a ring, and what we institute is keeping God's commandments, so that you stay far from all of that.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:48
precepts.why:
Christ says it plainly: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” You see it right there in red. For those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence: this is Christ himself speaking.

That is the wondrous thing the psalmist asks to behold: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” When I keep God’s commandments, the wondrous thing I see out of them is that he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him, perfect as our Father in heaven is perfect.

Those eyes are not only the bodily eyes. They are the spiritual eyes, the insight to see this word and the situation we are in, and to understand that it is all spiritual. That is why we have to delve into the scriptures and meditate, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law, and after we understand and observe, apply it and be like our Father.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:2
precepts.why:
This is what Christ’s words meant in the Old Testament. The Lord told Moses: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.” God is holy, and he says, you shall be holy.

Holiness is us coming into perfection. That is the wondrous thing out of God’s law in Psalms 119:18: the law is given so that his children can become like him.

What makes us perfect? Read on in Psalms 19. “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” The sun, the moon and the stars prove there must be a God; but how much more should you show him in your conversation and your actions, by not sinning? Then: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. The law is perfect because God’s laws are his ways, his habits, and he gave them unto his children. It converts us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for the redemption of our souls.

Then: “the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were simple, lost through slavery and oppression, calling ourselves anything but who we are. Coming back to understanding that we are the Israelites, and striving for perfection by keeping the law, is our souls being converted. And you cannot come to perfection without trials: gold is tried in the fire.

thread.text: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!

classes.title: Members of the Body  Pt2
Forged by Fire

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 25:1
precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Some think this is just talking about a bunch of Negroes coming together, a bunch of brothers together, and that's beautiful. No, it is much more than that. If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not gang banging, not the Hoovers, not the Omegas, Kappas and Alphas, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly nonsense some of us came out of. It is being unified in Christ; hence the name Israel United in Christ.

Sirach shows what unity God is beautified by: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren in what? In righteousness. The love of neighbours is not that oogly googly feeling, that's my neighbor, we're good friends; it is unity in righteousness, someone that shows care for their nation and their people. A man and a wife that agree together, in righteousness: a sanctified holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before the Lord.

Anything other than that is not beautiful, and the Lord is not beautified by it. Remember how Paul wrote to the different schools: you are puffed up, there are all types of schisms among you. That is not unity. To be unified means to come together in holiness and righteousness, the way God meant it to be and the way Christ told us to be. And that unification of the nation of Israel is the highest known threat to this evil world; it scares them.

precepts.label: Titus 1:13
precepts.why:
“A true witness delivereth souls”: a true prophet, a true servant, delivers souls. Paul shows how a true witness does it: “This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith.”

It is our job, brothers, to rebuke our people sharply. Why? That they may be sound in the faith; that they may repent. That is how souls are delivered.

So whose soul have you been delivering? You have been sitting here five years, seven years, ten years; some of you cannot even deliver your own soul, because you forgot the mission. Who are you working for, spiritually: Messiah or Satan? Some of you are agents working for Esau.

“but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.” Our people love lies, and the deceitful witness feeds them lies. That is why you see ten thousand, twenty thousand in the Christian churches: they do not want the truth. They say Christ cannot be black, Christ cannot come only for the Israelite. The truth to us is a foreign language. That is why the true witness has to rebuke sharply: sharp rebuke is what brings a people who love lies to repentance.

precepts.label: Romans 8:29
precepts.why:
“In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence.” Some of you have no confidence and low self-esteem because you have no fear of God, sitting in the same seat for seven years. Romans shows what God called you for: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

What does it mean to be conformed? To change. We must change to the image of Jesus Christ. Some of you have not changed yet, and we can see it.

We can see the potential on you: this brother has the spirit to do great things in Israel. But you have to see it. My job as a deacon is to push your spirit and to build you up, but no matter how much I build you up, if you cannot see it, I cannot make you see it. You have to get up and see it yourself.

There is a lot of work to do while you are waiting for the kingdom, and the kingdom does not come by observation. When temptation and tribulation come, the one who has not been conformed will run, because mentally and spiritually he is not strong enough to endure it. Being predestinated to be conformed means you have to do the changing.

precepts.label: Ephesians 1:5
precepts.why:
“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.” The same God who foreknew us and predestinated us to be conformed to the image of his Son predestinated us unto the adoption of children, by Jesus Christ, to himself.

That calling is what the class carried straight into Paul: “For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Paul understood he was a servant, sent to serve the people and deliver souls. Destruction unto me if I do not do what I was sent to do.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” You have to do it willingly, not because somebody forced you; a brother forced to do something has no spirit in it. Yet some of you get up at four in the morning and willingly give the white man eight or twelve hours without complaining, while coming here on the Sabbath is a burden.

So being predestinated as children by Jesus Christ is not a reason to sit and wait. God did not call you here just to sit and listen. It is a call to be the true witness that delivers souls, and in the fear of the Lord is the strong confidence to do it.

You are wandering away from God. You keep doing the same thing over and over and over and wonder why life is not working out for you. This is what spiritual men and women are supposed to examine: things aren't working right right now; could it be that you have a secret life?

But there has to be a day we stop, or we won't receive the kingdom.

precepts.label: Proverbs 23:33
precepts.why:
“Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way”: guard your heart and your mind in these commandments and these laws. Jump down the same chapter and see what happens to the heart that is not guided: “Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.”

Your eyes behold an evil woman, and your heart begins to utter. Does your heart utter anything? You utter from your mouth. So your eye is connected to your mind, and your mind is connected to your mouth. You see, you entertain, and then you begin to talk: hey, let me get your number, what's going on? Now you're talking, and you have no self-control over your members. Eye, mind, mouth. Out of the abundance of your heart your mouth speaks. No control, and then you're caught up.

It is the same road envy travels in verse 17, “Let not thine heart envy sinners”. Young people see the rapper's house, the girls, the car; the eyes instruct the mind, and the mind begins to envy: I want that, I want to be part of that. When you entertain it, you're telling God, that's what I choose, and this book isn't important. That is why we went into captivity: we did not serve the Lord with joyfulness and gladness of heart for the abundance of all things.

So guide thine heart in the way. Turn the eyes away before the mind takes hold and the mouth follows; that is self-control, and it keeps you in the fear of the Lord all the day long.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 3:16
precepts.why:
God is “declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done.” Only the God of Israel can do that, and he shows the end to the prophets. Look at the videos of the missiles coming down at night: don't they look like stars falling from heaven? The prophets had never seen a missile, an Iron Dome, a supersonic missile or a nuclear weapon. They described what they saw to the best of their ability, and it is our job to put it together. Put yourself in the prophet's shoes, because you are the prophets; you just don't remember.

Habakkuk describes how it hurts when these missiles hit, because when they hit they bring destruction. You don't want to be around when a missile hits the ground; you don't even want to be ten feet away.

“When I heard, my belly trembled.” That kind of fear is an anxiety sitting inside you, in your chest. He cannot believe what he is watching, but the Lord had to show it to him. “My lips quivered at the voice”: he was shaking, he couldn't even talk straight. “Rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself.” He could not believe the damage this thing was doing, the number of people it killed when it hit.

“That I might rest in the day of trouble.” He is saying, I don't want to be alive to see this. It is so bad I don't want to be around to see it. That is what Psalms 91 means by a thousand falling at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand: he saw the bomb drop and ten thousand people die right there.

That is the end God declared from the beginning, and “My counsel shall stand.” The media say Hamas is finished, Hezbollah has no weapons, Iran is weak; yet Hezbollah fired a hundred missiles into Israel the other day, and Israel cannot destroy Hamas under its nose while Iran is seven times bigger than Israel. We are going with the Bible. If you want the kingdom of heaven, you must accept what comes with it: war, tribulation and death.

precepts.label: Micah 2:11
precepts.why:
“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine.” We are an afflicted people, and we haven’t realized it yet. We are being put through the wringer because we constantly break his law of commandments, because we departed from God, because we don’t know who we are, and because God has been calling us and we refuse to turn around and come back to him. “If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” We are drunk with philosophy and doctrines, the lies we learned here in America. A lot of these wicked and evil pastors are just chasing money, money, money, and don’t give a damn about the people’s souls or their spirits. They don’t care about healing the people, fixing the people and bringing them back to Christ. The people are crying, looking for Christ, and these men mislead them while chasing the dollar bill. Let those men be your prophet if you are going to believe that garbage.

That is why we have gangs in the street, prostitutes in the street, our sons fainted and lying “at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”: the dead Israelites in the churches are not teaching our people how to keep the Lord’s commandments or how to come back to Christ. But the Lord who “pleadeth the cause of his people” says he has taken the cup of trembling out of our hand, and “I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee.”

They ignorantly call us YNs, and we call ourselves YNs, uncs and OGs, but that ain't your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings?

So the Lord says, “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors. When we bethink ourselves, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are. It is no longer, I'm a YN: we have young prophets amongst us. We are raising up our sons and daughters, young men, teens and young adults, in the understanding that they are the children of the prophets, the sons and daughters of God.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What our fathers went through was written for our learning, to increase our faith. When you learn from the examples of our ancestors, it gives us a guide for how we need to be today. That's called legacy.

How did our ancestors handle famine, persecution and tribulation? Job lost his children and his wealth and was covered in boils, and he said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Abraham was called to go out and “went out, not knowing whither he went”, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. We are going to have to get back to that, and who else did it but us? We are them; they are us.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:2
precepts.why:
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?” The heart is the mind, and nothing is more deceitful than the mind. Christ showed what comes out of it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

Yet Solomon says, “All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes”. Every one of us thinks we are righteous. Ask them: me? I ain't do nothing. Covetous spirit? Hatred? Oh, no. Judas would have said the same. All our ways are clean in our own eyes.

“but the Lord weigheth the spirits.” The Lord sees everything, and you cannot hide from the Most High. You can fool the deacon, you can fool the bishop and the leadership, but the Most High sees you, and you are not fooling yourself either. You know where you were last night, why you never called the brother back, and why you told her to hush before you answered the phone.

That is Jeremiah 17:10: “I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins”. Only God can search the mind, and he weighs what is really in it, not what we show each other. Read on: “Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established.”

precepts.label: Romans 8:27
precepts.why:
“I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.” Most of us only see each other on the Sabbath, and when we come around each other we are on our best behaviour. Six days a week, Sunday to Friday, we do not know where you are or what you are doing. So what are you doing when you are not here? The sister in Georgia bowed, said shalom and happy Sabbath for ten years while carrying on with the Uber Eats driver. She thought she was fooling us, and surely thought she was fooling the Most High. You cannot fool the Most High.

Paul says the same: “And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit”. The one who searches the heart is searching the mind. And that verse tells you there are two: the spiritual and the physical man. There is a war, the spirit against the flesh, wicked against righteous, darkness against light.

That war will never be over until Christ comes back or you die in this. Some want it to be over and ask why there is so much evil in their head. Maybe because you are not reading enough. Brothers who do not know the scriptures will be the ones to betray you, because when they come to him he will fall. Ask yourself when the brother you talk to during the week last talked scripture with you. The Lord searching the heart gives every man according to his ways: not the deacon's way or the bishop's way, but yours. You are your own biggest enemy.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:15-16
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face. Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you”. This is our deliverance from Babylon: we go back into the wilderness, Christ deals with us and teaches us the laws again, and what he is doing to us there is purging.

So what kind of pleading is he going to be doing? Is it baby, baby, please? No. The pleading is killing and smiting, and Isaiah proves it: “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh”. It's not a damn R&B song.

That is the same fury Ezekiel speaks of: “surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you”. As he pleaded with our fathers in the wilderness of Egypt, where the rebellious fell, he will plead with us, by fire and by the sword.

So even after the deliverance there is still going to be a purge. There will still be bad actors among us, people that still need to get right, and they are going to get it; Christ is the one who will give it to them.

precepts.label: Joel 3:2
precepts.why:
The Lord pleads with the nations the same way he pleads with Israel. Joel says: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel”. No baby, baby, please for them either. He will kill them, for his people Israel.

The nations are judged “for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” The pleading in the valley of Jehoshaphat is the Lord's vengeance on the ones who scattered us.

So when Ezekiel says the Lord will plead with Israel face to face in the wilderness “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”, the word means the same thing it means for the nations: judgment, smiting and fire, not begging. He pleads for Israel against the nations, and he pleads with the rebels in Israel in the wilderness, and nobody should read either as the Lord asking nicely.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:12
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says, “And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. What kind of purge is he going to be doing? Killing. Matthew shows it: “Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” Does anybody not understand that?

The wheat is gathered into the garner, and the chaff is burned. That is the rebels who “shall not enter into the land of Israel”. Zechariah is still talking about the purge: “in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” And even the third that is left still has to be sifted, refined, made right, purged.

The Lord is not going to give the kingdom to wicked negroes. The kingdom will not be open to wicked negroes. To get the kingdom you have to go through this fire and get right; there is no other way. You can't keep doing what you do and think you are going to get the kingdom. It is impossible.

That is why we have to fight for this and help each other. If I see you weak and say nothing to you, that means I hate you. So if I tell you, bro, you have to fix that, and you say I hate you, shut your ass up; I am trying to save your life. We are so used to not taking correction from each other that it feels like hate, because everybody has coddled you, and you keep kicking the can down the street until you are back on the corner doing what you do. The fan is already in his hand.

precepts.label: Additions to Esther 13:18
precepts.why:
“in their affliction they will seek me early.” God returns to his place, and our people have to seek him, but they have to be afflicted first. That is how our people are. And the afflictions are just starting. We have been getting killed in the street by police, but that ain't it; that is only the prelude to what is about to happen.

Esau is turning back the hands of the civil rights era right now, and that is good, because black people trust in their oppression. Memphis, maybe the blackest city in America, has been gerrymandered and carved up and parcelled out to the outskirts of the state so no black man can win a congressional seat there anymore, and it is happening in Texas and everywhere. An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers, protesting that he was an elected official and lawfully there. White guilt is out the window. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and they need the affliction, to see the devil for who he is.

In Esther's day: “All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes.” That is when our people are going to come: when death is before their eyes, they will cry earnestly and look for God. Right now they are still confused about who the devil is.

The church that once organized the community and planned the votes is silent while the civil rights laws are turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 with their organs taken out and it is called suicide. The only ones crying out about it are the Israelites. So it is our job to warn our people and bring them to repentance, and when they come with death before their eyes, we will show them what they are doing wrong and how to get right.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1-3
precepts.why:
Our people will cry earnestly when death is before their eyes, and Zephaniah says what to do before it comes: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” If you are seeking righteousness, you are admitting that you don't have it yet; you are walking in error and correcting it. So pray, Lord, show me where I am in error so I can fix it, so that when your decree brings forth I am lined up on the right side. That means when somebody is sent to tell you, this is wrong, you hear it and learn, because you don't want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

So when you come to the house of learning and somebody shows you your error, don't get mad and leave. Leaving means going back out there to face the fierce anger of God unprepared. While you are here, you are going to learn how to turn away from your sins.

As we see these afflictions happening, we know the judgment and the fierce anger of the Lord are coming. Our people are clueless about what is about to happen to them; in America we are so comfortable that hard living means cancelling Netflix. It is our job to warn them, and they have to be willing to listen and be gathered before the decree brings forth.

precepts.label: Amos 5:15
precepts.why:
Amos shows an Israel that hates the righteous: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.” They tread upon the poor, build houses of hewn stone and plant pleasant vineyards, “but ye shall not dwell in them”. Don't be comfortable, family; that is what Amos is saying. A few verses on he tells them what to hate instead: “Hate the evil, and love the good”.

David said, I love thy commandments, and I hate every false way. We hate anything outside of keeping God's commandments: sin. We are supposed to hate sin, hate the fact that there is sin in our community, and do something about it by keeping God's law. We are not supposed to tolerate evil amongst our people.

Love the good is love God's commandments. That is your purpose, it is what increases your faith, and it is why you are called to magnify God's law.

“And establish judgment in the gate”: establish judgment in yourself, your household, your nation and your communities. Then “it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.” You receive mercy when you hate the evil and love the good. That is the turn Amos calls for: stop hating the one who rebukes in the gate, and hate the sin instead. We separate ourselves from evil, the ways of our oppressor, and we strive for perfection.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 11:25
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. In that fire some want to quit, stop relying on the brotherhood and abandon ship. Sirach shows why: “In the day of prosperity there is a forgetfulness of affliction: and in the day of affliction there is no more remembrance of prosperity.”

In the day when things are going well, you forget what it was like to be in your lowest state, and you have to take heed lest you fall. And in the day of affliction, when the fire comes up and the heat gets turned up, you forget the prosperity: the last end, the increase the Lord is going to give you, the things he has in store.

The trying of your faith worketh patience, and Sirach 2 says, woe unto them that have lost patience. If you would just purge your spirit, you would be able to receive all the things the Lord has promised for the future. But you quit because you forgot what the goal was; you forgot the mission, so you want to abandon ship.

When you are going through that adversity, be patient in your lowest state and don't forget the prosperity to come. That is what strengthens your faith through the refining, until the Lord says, “It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

precepts.label: Matthew 24:10-13
precepts.why:
Zechariah says two parts shall be cut off and die and the third brought through the fire. We are still talking about the purge. Christ describes what the purge looks like among the people: “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.”

In this purging process a lot of people are going to turn their back to the Lord. That is what people forget: you are not turning your back to us. We are nothing but humble servants of the Lord, working together in the vineyard. You are turning your back to the Master and saying, I don't want to do the work anymore. And when you turn your back to your brother, it is called betrayal.

“And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many.” That is the one who says, I can do the work outside the body; I don't have to be here; I can do my own thing. If you were going to do the work somewhere else, why wouldn't you do it here and continue the mission? Because you were never going to do the work; you had no intentions of doing it. And they deceive the simple. A brand new fool with the Bishop's precept book starts his own thing, while leadership has laboured twenty-plus years to do this work, and other fools follow him.

“And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” Iniquity, the short word is sin. “But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” Fight until the end: that is the only way you get salvation. You have to walk through hell to get to heaven. There is no shortcut and no roundabout to the kingdom; you walk straight through. If you don't want to do it, don't do it.

precepts.label: James 5:16
precepts.why:
The Pharisees asked, “Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” Why is Christ sitting and communicating with ungodly people? To bring them to repentance. That was the whole purpose: “I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” So if you think you're right, then he's not here for you. The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

James shows that first step: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” You have to confess your faults so that we can pray for you and you can be healed. There is no healing without confession.

You can't cherry-pick what you want out of the Bible and expect to be received of God and Christ. Christ said, I came for the sick, those that need healing. But the sick have to own that they are sick. Many people are right in their own eyes; we don't want to see ourselves in a negative light and we act like the parts of us that aren't right will be all right with God. We will fall short of the kingdom if we keep that mindset of not changing.

So confession is where the physician's work begins. The one who acknowledges his faults can be prayed for and healed; the one who hides them, looking the part with fringes and a beard, stays sick.

precepts.label: Psalms 107:20
precepts.why:
Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” He came for the sick, those that need healing. So what do we use to heal ourselves? The psalm answers: “He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.”

He sent his word down to heal them. Write that down. The word of God is the medicine the physician brings.

So, men, do you know what the will of God is? Then you are ahead of the whole world, because people out here are crazy. People think you can still eat pork, or whatever you do, vote for Trump, whatever people are doing in this world. But you know his word, and his word is what is going to heal.

That is how the sinners at Christ's table were to be made whole: not by sacrifices, but by receiving the word he sent and letting it deliver them from their destructions. We all come in here sick, and we need to get cured.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:69
precepts.why:
Ezra speaks of God “being judge”, and of those “that are cured with his word.” Cured with his word: that is why Christ said, I didn't come for the righteous, I came for the sick, and I am going to give them my word so they can be healed and cured.

Read on and Ezra shows what would happen if God did not forgive those who are cured by his word and put out the multitude of contentions: “There should be very few left peradventure in an innumerable multitude.” Out of all the multitude, hardly any would be left.

So the word of God will cure you; it will heal you. When James says, confess your faults one to another and pray for one another that you may be healed, we have to apply the word of God. That is the cure the physician gives to sinners.

And that is the meaning of “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” We used to give sacrifices to absolve us for the sins we committed, but that is not how it was supposed to be from the beginning. The Lord said, I want to see you change rather than keep on sacrificing. His mercy is for those who are cured with his word and actually change.

precepts.label: Luke 22:31-34
precepts.why:
God said, “Behold, I send my messenger before thy face”: John, sent to teach the people and get them right to prepare for Christ. That is the job of the prophet, the apostle and every teacher: to show you. Then Christ called Simon and Andrew, James and John, from their nets. These men came in to get right, and do you think that walking with him he was not showing them all their errors? Luke shows him doing it with Peter.

“And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you get right, then go strengthen your brethren. Christ is showing Peter he still has things to work on. You want to walk with me? I'm going to show you what your problems are.

Peter answered, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.” And Christ said, “I tell thee, Peter”, didn't you just hear what I said to you? “the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.” Peter, you ain't there yet. Your mind ain't right yet. Get converted first.

Peter did become the head of the church afterwards, but first there were things he had to reconcile within himself. God opens his book and we behold ourselves in it; he sends prophets to show us how to get right. The worst thing to do is deny it. It don't feel good when you're going through it, but it's good for you. Medicine hurts sometimes, but if you are sincere you take your medicine and you get better. If you don't, you become an example of what not to do.

And those who teach must turn it on themselves too: don't weaponize the scriptures to correct everybody else while you can't see your own flaws, or hold brothers to a perfection you yourself are far from.

precepts.why:

The hatred you carry is equivalent to murder. Where does it all begin? In your mind, as Mark 7 says. Before you ever commit the act of physical murder, it has to begin with a thought, and the thought of it is the exact same thing. The hatred we have as a people one for another: God says you're already a murderer. You already broke the commandment thou shalt not kill.

It works the same with adultery. The minute you see that ex at the grocery store and take his phone number, before you have even said anything, that is adultery right there. It starts in the mind.

Nobody knows you more than Messiah. He created you, so he knows what is in your mind. We cannot read your mind, but he can, and “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” So deal with the hatred while it is still a thought, because no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:20-21
precepts.why:
“Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” Christ says “The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” What is that really saying? Isaiah shows it.

“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.” That word you hear, this is the way, walk ye in it, is how you are born. That is how you are born of the spirit.

The wind that blows where it will is the word of God. You don't know who the word of God is going to affect. The sound thereof is “This is the way, walk ye in it”, the word of God. Every last one of us in here heard the truth, heard that sound, heard that call, and it activated us. The Lord has his agents on the earth, like sleeper cells: you just hear a certain trigger word behind you and you activate, you wake up to this truth. The Bible is the activation.

And notice what comes with it: the bread of adversity and the water of affliction. A brother is born for adversity. When you are born into this truth and depart from evil, you make yourself a prey; Satan comes for you, and you will have to go through things. But the teachers are no longer hid in a corner, and the word behind you keeps you walking in the way.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1-2
precepts.why:
The believers in Acts 4 “were of one heart and of one soul” and “had all things common”. To keep from losing ourselves, selling ourselves out and losing our souls, we have to grow the same way. Paul shows what pulls us away: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”.

The seducing spirits are money and wealth, the many things that distract us from God, from Christ and from our purpose in life. We live in an era where vanity is a drug and attention is a drug. At the blitz last week, kids said they want to be streamers. What about a plumber, a mechanic, a builder, an architect, a lawyer, an engineer, the things that actually build nations? That is why we have been destroyed as a people. And there are men and women in the faith who want to leave this and go to the world and stream.

The “doctrines of devils” are religion, man-made religion. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy” is politics: a lie that makes you feel assimilated into a government that is kicking you out of it. If you are Israel, what they call black, you cannot be in their government. There is one black governor in this whole country, and all the black generals have been taken out as not qualified. They are making their country great again in their eyes.

“Having their conscience seared with a hot iron.” Religion, politics and the gifts of this world sear the conscience. Money, riches and comfort should not be your god; the American dream is a lie. Having all things in common, in faith and understanding, is what keeps us from departing from the faith.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 3:1-5
precepts.why:
“This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.” In perilous times we have to start having all things in common, like the believers of Acts 4, and build our faith.

“For men shall be lovers of their own selves”: going for likes, not worried about being an aid to your society or your community. It is me, me, me: how many likes and followers do I have? It is not about you, negro. It is about your people. “Covetous, boasters”: boasting of vanity, money, drugs, houses, cars, women. “Proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful”: not appreciative of God and what he has done for you. “Unholy, Without natural affection”.

This is the nature of them that go after the world, that go after the gift that destroys the heart. The one who is a lover of himself holds on to what he has; the believers in Acts 4 said none of the things they possessed was their own.

So we have to stop living beyond our means and be content with our wages and content in life. A family of seven may need a house with a little room, but if you are a single brother, why are you buying a mansion and expensive cars? Do you know the times we are living in? There is coming a time when you will not be worrying about maintaining your BMW. Riches and comfort, keeping up with the Joneses and the American lie of a dream, should not be your god.

precepts.label: Acts 4:34-35
precepts.why:
The same chapter shows what having all things common looked like: “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

That is the point. We have to begin to live below our means, not beyond them. This nation of ours is a big nation, and there are millions of our people that lack. When you sacrifice your much, it is much to them that have little.

The only way to experience that, to let what you have help those who have little, is to travel. We must go and spread this gospel abroad, and that is part of why we go out into the nations.

The believers of Acts 4 had prayed, the place was shaken, and they were filled with the Holy Ghost and spake the word with boldness. Out of that came one heart and one soul, and out of one heart and one soul came a people among whom no one lacked. That is the same order we need now: faith first, and then a nation that looks after its own.

precepts.label: Romans 8:26-30
precepts.why:
“Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.” That is the part of us that groans to God because we are expecting the kingdom, if we are sincere. We are asking God to deal with us: I want the kingdom, I don't want to come up short, Lord, please preserve me, help me. Then let the word be engrafted in your mind; he is telling you what to do.

“And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.”

“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God”. If you love God, you are keeping the commandments. It works for good to those keeping the commandments, those that have the word engrafted in them, “the called according to his purpose.”

“For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son”. Those that followed him before will follow him again; they are predestinated. You are going to be conformed to that image and measure to the fulness of the stature of Christ in this mortal body, because sin cannot reign in this mortal body. Stop thinking it is going to happen on the other side. Whoever could not figure out that you cannot live a life of sin and go to the kingdom is not going; they are going to be in the lake.

A hard word goes with it. Sisters that are married: if you refuse to serve your husband, look at him as your lord and obey him, down to the little things he tells you to do, you are not going, no matter how many head covers you wear or what offices you hold. If Jesus told you, you would do it. And husbands, if you are not guiding your wives in these scriptures and showing them how to be that woman, that is your fault; you are no wise master builder, having expectations while not molding them. Then the children are cursed. When a twelve-year-old in the house is deep in gay porn, something is wrong in that house, something is wrong with those parents.

precepts.label: Romans 8:19-21
precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death”. The payment for sin is death. “but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord”. Through Christ is eternal life, and that is what we are looking for. If we keep the commandments, God says he is going to give us the kingdom, so we are expecting the kingdom.

Romans 8 shows that expectation: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” The creature “was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope”, “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” That is what our expectation is to be: delivered out of bondage into the liberty of the children of God.

Then if we know the wages of sin is death, why sin? If you live in sin you are not expecting this; you know what you are going to get. In that day you will be saying Lord, Lord, and he will say, I don't know you; you didn't do what I said to do. How do you expect something you did not do?

So if your expectation is to be called a son of God in the kingdom, do not let sin reign in this mortal body. The one living a life of sin and thinking he will go to the kingdom is not going; he will be in the lake.

precepts.label: Romans 12:21
precepts.why:
The first step is study, pray and apply: do your research, and then turn from sin. Then we have to learn how to turn all of this evil and mischief into righteousness, from the power of Satan to God, from darkness unto light. Romans 12 lays out the steps: “Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.” Come home, family.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another”: looking out for each other and honoring one another within our marriages, our relationships and our nation. “Not slothful in business”: our business is that we are called by God to magnify the law and increase our faith. “Fervent in spirit; serving the Lord”: doing the work and helping your people. “Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; Distributing to the necessity of saints”. What better life to live than to help your people?

And the chapter ends with the sum of it: “Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.” Do not let this world destroy your faith.

How do we overcome? With the good of these commandments and the faith of Christ, and knowing who you are. You overcome that evil with the good of this Bible. Love without dissimulation, brotherly love, fervency, patience and prayer are the good that overcomes the evil around us.

precepts.label: Romans 8:13-14
precepts.why:
It is not a sin to drink. But when we use drinking as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into condemnation; it is not to be used in that manner. When we are dealing with issues, we always have to rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome these things.

“For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die”. To live after the flesh is to obey the elements of the flesh: going to the bottle and making that the outlet. The end of that road is always death, just as Habakkuk 2:12 shows that there is always an evil road, and at the end of it you find death.

“but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live”. That is where we are. The drinking problem in this land is a quarter trillion dollars, but the commandments fix all of that.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.” That is how we are to be. So we should not be overcome with that evil; we have to overcome that evil with good, and the good is God's laws.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 31:28-29
precepts.why:
“Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind”. Measurably. The wine is not the sin; the measure is the key. “But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind”. That is the key point: bitterness of the mind.

The Lord cannot use you if you do not have that balance. Every element on the earth was created by the Lord, and it has its function and its purpose. But if you use it and abuse it, you cannot be useful for the nation.

It is the same with alcoholism as it is with food, which the Bishop has been bringing out: all of it has a balance, and if you overuse it you fall. Our oppressors are depending on us to lose that balance. That is why you have the KFCs across the street from Domino's, and the liquor stores in our neighborhoods: they are depending on you to fall into that destruction, that chaos, that confusion.

Nobody out there is drinking measurably or sociably; it is used to drown out reality, and it will kill you. So overcoming evil with good means holding the balance the Most High set in every element, and not letting the bottle become the outlet.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 5:15
precepts.why:
Paul opens, “Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant.” Sirach says the same: “Be not ignorant of any thing in a great matter or a small.” You have to learn this and understand it, in the great matters as well as the small.

Do not be ignorant in the functionings of this body. It is essential to understand how the body works: you have to realize what every individual is worth. Nobody is above this. You are special because you are part of the body, but do not think you are more than another part. We are all one, working towards the same goal, and we have to do exactly what the Lord told us to do to get where we need to get.

It is easy to come in, sit down, and think everybody is just doing what they do. But understand how intricate this thing is, how many different offices there are in this body. Some came in, got patted down, dropped the kids off, and did not think twice about how much goes into dealing with those children. Some will get a plate of food brought to them and have no idea how many hands were involved to make that plate possible. There are people with gifts to deal with things you do not even have to think about. Be not ignorant of that.

precepts.label: Romans 12:2
precepts.why:
To be not ignorant, Paul tells the Romans: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. When you come into this truth you are supposed to transform the way you think. The scriptures are supposed to be inside you now, and you have to apply them.

And why? “that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” To prove means you are not ignorant. It is the ability to process, to identify, to differentiate. Your antennas are up now, and you will not be ignorant in anything any longer.

You were ignorant in the church. You were dumb as hell, stupid, knowing nothing, just walking along the line doing what everybody was doing: it is Christmas time, it is somebody's birthday, Mother's Day, Father's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, and never asking why. But now you are different. Now it has to make sense: what does the scripture say, where is that in the Bible? That is proving what is acceptable unto the Most High God, his perfect will.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
What is the will of the Lord? David answers: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God, and they are within the heart.

That is what a renewed mind does with them: it moves by them, processes, understands, knows, sees clearly. You have understanding now, and you are bouncing things off of the scriptures.

So you no longer conform to this world. You do not move like everybody else anymore. You are using your mind for what it is for: to delight in doing the will of God, with his law written within your heart. That is the opposite of the ignorance Paul warned the Corinthians about when he wrote, “I would not have you ignorant.”

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:13
precepts.why:
You have one job on this earth, and you have been given a mind to do that job. Solomon gives it: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” One duty.

You have a brain to understand how to fear God. You have a brain to understand what the commandments of God are. You have a brain to apply the laws of God in your life. That is why you have a mind. Congratulations: you know the meaning of life now.

If you are doing anything else with your mind, you missed. You are on that broad road to destruction. You cannot fill your mind with kill moves on Mortal Kombat, the moves on the PlayStation, the stats of Kobe and whether the NBA finals are over. We don't give a damn about none of that. Fill your mind with thus saith the Lord. Apply it to what is necessary in life: How do I deal with my wife? How do I deal with my kids? What can I do to become stronger, a better asset in this truth, so the Lord can use me? That is what we are supposed to be concerned with. If you are concerned with something else, maybe this ain't you.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:19-21
precepts.why:
Following what the Deacon brought out, Christ says: “For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.” Wherever your treasure is, that is where your mind is going to be occupied.

If your mind is filled with Mortal Kombat moves and the stats of the greatest to ever play any sport, that is where your focus is and that is where you are building up your treasures. “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. All of those carnal things are going to be destroyed, so that should not be where your focus is.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt”. When you occupy your mind in the laws of God, that is where you are laying up your treasure: how to unify, how can I be used as a tool for the Lord's army, how can I be utilized to push this truth further. That is where our minds should be: on treasure that cannot be corrupted, that no rust or moth can touch.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:18-19
precepts.why:
“Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” Why does Paul bring this up before he goes over the order of the body? Because they were not accustomed to godly order or sound doctrine. They were following dumb idols, doing what those idols wanted instead of what the Most High God wanted. He tells the Ephesians the same: “remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh”. That was us too: Hellenized, living like heathens.

Think about the mind frame of a person that follows idols. Habakkuk: “What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?” Somebody created this thing, formed it, and then turned around and said this is God, this is what brought you out of Egypt. You know how dumb you have to be? You stupid.

“Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach!” Woe is destruction: destruction to him that says to the wooden idol, wake up, and to the dumb stone, arise. You are on a highway to hell, a fast track to destruction, following dumb idols.

That is why Paul reminds them of the mindset they came from: to teach organization to a Hellenized Jew is extremely difficult. You have to let them know, that is not us anymore. As Romans 12 says, you have to renew your mind. We do not conduct ourselves like that any longer; now we learn the order of the body of Christ.

precepts.label: 1 John 5:21
precepts.why:
Paul reminds the Corinthians where they came from: “Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” John gives the charge that goes with it: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” Stay the heck away from them. Stay away from it.

This was us. Esau's successful mission was to make our nation forget the laws of God and change the ordinances, to take away our heritage and make us become something we are not. They created that mind frame here, and you see it amongst our people.

Once you come into the truth you are supposed to go ten times harder and repent, not go back to the idols you were carried away to. Habakkuk showed where the idol worshipper ends up: destruction, speaking to wood and dumb stone that cannot teach.

So Paul clears away the old idol mindset before he teaches the diversities of gifts, administrations and operations in the one body. Keep yourselves from idols, renew your mind, and you can learn the godly order the Most High set in his body.
